title: In vitro fluorescence binding assay for gSTEP biosensor Kd determination
summary: Measure the equilibrium dissociation constant (Kd) and fractional fluorescence change (ΔF/F0) between a gSTEP fluorescent-biosensor variant and its binding partner by titrating the partner against a fixed concentration of gSTEP in a 96-well plate and fitting the fluorescence response to a ligand-depletion Hill equation.
source_citation: Eason et al., ACS Synth. Biol. 2020, DOI 10.1021/acssynbio.0c00407

materials.name: Purified gSTEP variant protein (His-tagged, IMAC-purified, buffer-exchanged)
materials.provenance_note: 75 nM final per well is stated in the source.

materials.name: Binding partner (titrant): STEPtag
materials.provenance_note: User selected STEPtag as the target from the paper's reported partners (STEPtag / TAX-L10-STEPtag / STEPtag-L10-TAX).

materials.name: Control protein: bovine serum albumin (BSA)
materials.provenance_note: BSA named as a control protein in the source; inactive TAX (E157A/E263A) is the stated alternative.

equipment: Microcentrifuge tubes or a dilution plate for the titrant serial dilution

steps.title: Prepare assay buffer
steps.instruction: Prepare 20 mM sodium phosphate buffer containing 50 mM NaCl and adjust to pH 7.4. Filter-sterilize. This is both the protein storage buffer and the assay diluent.

critical_parameters.name: Buffer composition
critical_parameters.value: 20 mM sodium phosphate, 50 mM NaCl, pH 7.4

steps.title: Prepare fixed-concentration gSTEP working solution
steps.instruction: Dilute purified gSTEP variant to 75 nM in assay buffer. Prepare enough for every well plus dead volume.

critical_parameters.name: gSTEP working-solution volume
critical_parameters.provenance_note: Scaling: 12 titrant points x 3 replicates x 2 (target + control) = 72 wells; 72 wells x 100 uL/well = 7.2 mL, +10% dead volume = ~8 mL. Verify against your plate layout.

warnings: Keep gSTEP on ice and protected from light until dispensed to limit photobleaching.

steps.title: Prepare the titrant serial dilution series
steps.instruction: Prepare a serial dilution series of the binding partner (STEPtag) spanning the expected Kd, plus a matched series of the control protein (BSA). Twelve points is a good default.

critical_parameters.name: Titrant concentration range
critical_parameters.provenance_note: User chose a Kd-relative range (recommended default). Requires an estimate of the expected Kd (from a pilot or the paper's reported values); flag to verify once Kd is known.

critical_parameters.name: Number of titration points
critical_parameters.provenance_note: 12-point, 2-fold serial dilution is standard for a well-resolved binding isotherm.

substeps.instruction: Set the top concentration to ~10x the expected Kd; perform 2-fold serial dilutions down to ~0.1x Kd.
substeps.provenance_note: Standard titration spacing to bracket the Kd.

substeps.instruction: Prepare an identical dilution series of the control protein (BSA) to define nonspecific/background fluorescence change.
substeps.provenance_note: Control titration implied by the source's use of a control protein.

warnings: If the expected Kd is unknown, run a wide pilot range first (e.g., 1 nM to 10 uM) and refine.

steps.title: Assemble the plate
steps.instruction: Into each well of a Fluotrac 96-well plate, combine gSTEP at 75 nM final with one titrant concentration, in assay buffer, to the chosen well volume. Include the control-protein titration and buffer-only blank wells. Run each condition in at least three replicates.

critical_parameters.name: Assay volume per well
critical_parameters.provenance_note: User selected 100 uL/well (scale choice; not specified in the source).

critical_parameters.name: Blank wells
critical_parameters.provenance_note: Blank and gSTEP-only wells define F0 and background; standard practice for ΔF/F0.

warnings: Mix gently and avoid bubbles, which corrupt fluorescence reads.

steps.title: Equilibrate
steps.instruction: Incubate the assembled plate to allow binding to reach equilibrium before reading.

critical_parameters.name: Equilibration time and temperature
critical_parameters.provenance_note: Not stated in the source. User accepted the standard-practice default (equilibrium binding at controlled temperature). The ligand-depletion Hill fit assumes equilibrium, so this is outcome-critical — verify equilibrium is reached for your Kd/kinetics.

warnings: If on/off kinetics are slow relative to 30 min, extend the equilibration or the fitted Kd will be biased.

steps.title: Read fluorescence
steps.instruction: Read gSTEP fluorescence for every well on the Tecan Infinite M1000 with excitation at 485 nm and emission at 515 nm.

critical_parameters.name: Reader gain / bandwidth
critical_parameters.value: optimize on a high-signal well; keep fixed across the plate
critical_parameters.provenance_note: Not stated. Set gain once on a bound (high-signal) well and hold it constant; verify no wells saturate.

steps.title: Fit Kd and ΔF/F0
steps.instruction: For each titration, subtract the control-protein background, then fit gSTEP fluorescence intensity as a function of titrant concentration to the ligand-depletion form of the Hill equation to extract Kd and ΔF/F0. Report mean +/- s.d. across replicates.

critical_parameters.name: Fitting model
critical_parameters.value: Hill equation accounting for ligand depletion
critical_parameters.provenance_note: The source specifies this fit (and cites its reference 35). Use total, not free, concentrations because ligand depletion is modeled.

warnings: Ligand depletion matters when Kd is comparable to protein concentration (75 nM here) — do not substitute a free-ligand Hill fit.

assumptions_log.basis: User picked STEPtag from the paper's reported partners.
Scaling from 72 wells x 100 uL + 10% dead volume; depends on your plate layout.
Kd-relative range chosen by user; needs an expected-Kd estimate.
12-point 2-fold series is standard for a resolved isotherm.
Scale choice; not specified in the source.
Standard controls to define F0 and background for ΔF/F0.
Standard equilibrium-binding practice; the source omits it and the fit assumes equilibrium.
Not stated; set on a high-signal well and keep constant across the plate.

open_questions: Expected Kd is required to set the titrant range concretely; run a wide pilot (e.g., 1 nM to 10 uM) if unknown.
Equilibration time (30 min) is a best-practice default, not measured for this system; confirm binding has reached equilibrium given the on/off kinetics.
Path-length / inner-filter effects at 100 uL in a 96-well plate are not corrected; verify signal is linear with gSTEP concentration.

On a live run, Phase-2 web_search would attempt to ground equilibration time, titrant spacing, and the ligand-depletion Hill model in specific citations (upgrading these from best_practice/default_verify to verified literature_grounded).
